Test Information

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

The Anti-CCP hs (high sensitive)® test quantitatively detects autoantibodies against specific epitopes of MCV (mutated citrullinated vimentin). It is thus a highly sensitive and very specific laboratory test for the diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis.

Anti-CCP hs (high sensitive)® is based on selected and optimized peptide epitopes from the body’s own protein MCV.

Together with rheumatoid factor, autoantibodies against citrullinated antigens (ACPA) have been included as determining factors in the current ACR criteria for the classification of rheumatoid arthritis. The introduction of Anti-CCP hs (high sensitive)® makes available an ACPA test that allows for the diagnosis of RA with at least comparable sensitivity and significantly higher specificity and prognostic power than with conventional rheumatoid factors.

Interpretation :

 

This test is used for the semi-quantitative determination of the IgG class of auto antibodies specific to CCP in biological specimens.

Detection of anti-CCP antibodies is used as an aid in the diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis and should be used in conjunction with

other clinical information. Autoantibody levels represent one parameter in a multi criterion diagnostic process, encompassing both

clinical and laboratory based assessments.
